original_statement:
What did you do? List the exact steps to reproduce, in order. Run aspergillus's check-duplicates against a codebase containing near-miss or semantic duplicates (type-3/type-4 clones): two functions that share a substantial copied spine — a verbatim-identical inner closure plus an identical call, and duplicated statement sequences — embedded in two structurally different functions. (Originally observed in exophial3 on src/e_new_model/shell/drive.py:drive vs src/e_new_model/shell/driver.py:put.)
What did you expect to happen? check-duplicates flags (a) type-3 near-miss/gapped clones (copied fragments inside differently-shaped functions with added/removed/changed statements) and (b) type-4 semantic clones (functionally equivalent, syntactically different code) — or at minimum states in its own docs that its scope is type-2-only.
What actually happened? Include the exact error text or output. The detector at python/src/aspergillus/duplicates.py normalizes each function body (identifiers -> _ID, literals -> type markers; _Normalizer), renders the whole normalized body, sha256-hashes it (_hash_function), and groups only functions whose ENTIRE normalized body hashes identically (find_duplicate_groups). Fragment-level near-miss (type-3) and semantically-equivalent-but-syntactically-different (type-4) matches never produce a hit, on any input, by construction of the whole-body-hash comparison; a substantial duplicated spine embedded in two differently-shaped functions yields 'no duplicate functions found'. duplicates.py's own docstring self-declares 'This is what makes the hash a type-2 clone signature'.
Which surface or component? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) aspergillus check-duplicates (python/src/aspergillus/duplicates.py: _Normalizer, _hash_function, find_duplicate_groups)
What environment and version? (OS, app/gateway build or commit, network) aspergillus repo, Python rule pack (python/)
Is it reproducible? (always / intermittently / once) — and how often. always
What is the impact / severity? Who is blocked and how badly? The duplication gate is scoped to type-2 (renamed whole-function) clones only. Type-3 near-miss/gapped clones and type-4 semantic clones pass the gate uncaught. Standard type-1..4 clone taxonomy (Roy & Cordy clone-detection survey; Bellon et al. clone-tool comparison).
What activity was underway when this was found? (ODC Activity — e.g. testing, code review, normal usage, reproduction attempt) design review
What condition or event exposed the defect? (ODC Trigger — e.g. a config change, concurrent access, a boundary/edge-case input, an unusual workload) design conformance
Which quality/capability dimension does this affect? (ODC Impact — e.g. reliability, usability, capability, performance, security, maintainability, standards, requirements — distinct from the severity/who's-blocked question above) maintainability

Decomposed child: Add type-1 (exact) clone detection to aspergillus's check-duplicates (python/src/aspergillus/duplicates.py), per the Roy & Cordy (2007) clone taxonomy: compare function bodies after stripping comments and whitespace only, with no identifier renaming and no literal normalization applied. Each detected type-1 pair in the report must carry its clone type label and a similarity score. Exclude boilerplate (trivial dunders/getters/pass-only bodies) from reports. Build a pytest suite covering type-1 fixtures drawn from the Roy & Cordy (2007) editing-scenario taxonomy and from Bellon et al. (2007) reference clones, asserting the detector correctly labels type-1 pairs.
restatement: Aspergillus's check-duplicates tool currently finds only type-2 clones: function bodies that hash the same after identifiers are collapsed to a placeholder and literals are collapsed to type markers. This request adds a second, stricter clone category: type-1 (exact) clones, defined by the Roy and Cordy (2007) clone taxonomy as function bodies that are identical once only comments and whitespace are stripped away, with no identifier renaming and no literal normalization applied. When the tool finds a type-1 pair, its report must show that pair's clone type label and a similarity score. The tool must not report boilerplate pairs — trivial dunder methods, one-line getters, or pass-only bodies — as clones, even when those pairs are identical. A pytest suite must be built and added to the project's test suite. That suite must cover type-1 fixtures drawn from the Roy and Cordy (2007) editing-scenario taxonomy and from the Bellon et al. (2007) reference-clone benchmark, and it must show that the tool labels type-1 pairs correctly.

restatement_clauses.text: The detector must implement type-1 (exact) clone detection per the Roy & Cordy (2007) clone taxonomy: it compares function bodies after stripping comments and whitespace only, with no identifier renaming and no literal normalization applied.
Each detected type-1 clone pair in the report must carry its clone type label and a similarity score.
The detector must exclude boilerplate (trivial dunders, getters, and pass-only bodies) from reports.

A pytest suite must be built covering type-1 fixtures drawn from the Roy & Cordy (2007) editing-scenario taxonomy and from Bellon et al. (2007) reference clones, asserting the detector correctly labels type-1 pairs.

goal: Add type-1 (exact) clone detection to aspergillus's check-duplicates tool, with a clone type label and similarity score on each reported pair, boilerplate excluded from reports, and a pytest suite grounded in the Roy and Cordy (2007) and Bellon et al. (2007) taxonomies proving it works.
acceptance_criteria: Two functions that differ only by comments and blank lines are marked as a type-1 clone pair. Two functions that differ only by renamed identifiers, and two functions that differ only by a changed literal value, are each NOT marked as a type-1 clone pair.
For a pair of functions that are identical except for comments and blank lines, the report labels the pair 'type-1' and gives it a similarity score of at least 0.95.

Two copies of a trivial dunder method, two copies of a one-line getter, and two copies of a pass-only method are never reported as clones. A genuine duplicated function with real logic is still reported.
A dedicated automated test file for type-1 clone detection exists in the project's test suite.
The new test file names both sources its fixtures are drawn from: Roy and Cordy's 2007 clone taxonomy paper, and Bellon and colleagues' 2007 reference-clone work.
The new test file contains at least 6 separate test cases, showing a real suite of fixtures rather than one token test.

Three separate pairs of functions — one that differs only by a blank line, one that differs only by an added comment, and one that differs only by spacing around an operator — are each correctly identified as type-1 clones.
